paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. Saul did part of the job and called it the whole job. The LORD said to devote everything to destruction, and Saul and his troops spared Agag and the best of the animals (1 Samuel 15:3, 9). Then Saul looked Samuel in the face and said, "I have carried out the LORD's instructions" (1 Samuel 15:13), while the sheep were bleating in the background. I've tried that with a cookie timer. The oven does not care how confident I sound.

Samuel's answer is the heart of it: "Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams" (1 Samuel 15:22). Saul kept pointing at what he wanted to give the LORD, but the LORD had asked for something else, which was to listen and do what He said. Saul even says why he did it: "I feared the people and obeyed their voice" (1 Samuel 15:24). That's the question for you and me, friend. Whose voice is the loudest one in the room when it's time to obey?

And look at how sorry sounds here. Saul says "I have sinned," but he follows it with a request to be honored before the elders and Israel (1 Samuel 15:30). I think he was worried about how he looked. Samuel, on the other hand, mourned for Saul (1 Samuel 15:35), and I think that tells us obeying God is no cold rule. So when you hear what God says, do all of it, not just the parts that feel good. The LORD sees the whole thing, and He's worth listening to.
